candidates.title: Stranded 'born-dead' building: demolished before ever opening
candidates.shift: A completed concert hall in Tbilisi is being demolished having never opened to the public — a finished structure that never entered operational life.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: an unsettling case of spec-construction risk with no category — what do insurers, lenders and cities call an asset that is built but never activated? Could apply to spec retail/mixed-use too.
candidates.evidence: TV Pirveli/Dezeen footage shows cladding removal and demolition underway on the never-opened Studio Fuksas-designed Rike Concert Hall in Tbilisi.
candidates.initial_analysis: This is an example of speculative civic/cultural construction becoming instantly obsolete before use — a shift from 'building as investment' to 'building as stranded liability.' If this pattern recurs, financiers may need a new risk category for never-activated structures.
candidates.author: Lizzie Crook

candidates.title: Public procurement as innovation lever in Amazon interior
candidates.shift: A study frames local-government purchasing power in the Brazilian Amazon interior as a deliberate tool for innovation and regional development, not neutral spend.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: periphery geography using procurement rules as an economic-development lever could preview policy templates for building supply-chain and construction capacity in other underserved regions.
candidates.evidence: Academic analysis of public procurement's contribution to innovation and local development in the interior of the Brazilian Amazon.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from procurement-as-spending to procurement-as-development-infrastructure. If it spreads, retailers and builders entering peripheral/remote markets may face government contracts explicitly designed to seed local construction and supply capacity.
candidates.author: Lidiane de Melo Araújo, Antônio do Socorro Ferreira Pinheiro, Enio Erasmo de Oliveira Ramalho

candidates.title: Absence: no software category bridges ERP/WMS and physical shelf reality
candidates.shift: A supply-chain framework paper argues standard ERP/WMS/TMS architectures consistently fail to capture the physical, on-shelf complexity of food/FMCG/FMCD retail.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: names a genuine absence — no established category yet closes the gap between digital inventory systems and physical shelf-presence, an opening for computer-vision-linked shelf tools.
candidates.evidence: Conceptual framework paper noting ERP/WMS/TMS limits when confronted with physical shelf-presence complexity in food, FMCG and FMCD supply chains.
candidates.source: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
candidates.initial_analysis: Points to a shift from software-modeled inventory to physically-verified inventory. If unaddressed, retailers may increasingly need computer-vision or physical-AI shelf-sensing layered atop legacy WMS/ERP systems — a cross-branch convergence of supply chain and tech.
candidates.author: Santanu Mukherjee

candidates.title: AI-stabilized waste-to-energy edges toward store-level circularity
candidates.shift: AI control systems are being applied to overcome instability and feedstock heterogeneity in anaerobic digestion/waste-to-energy, potentially making small-scale on-site conversion more viable.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if AI stabilizes small digesters, grocery/food-court organic waste could become an on-site energy source, changing utility and waste-hauling arrangements for stores.
candidates.evidence: Review on AI-driven optimization of anaerobic digestion and waste-to-energy systems addressing process instability and heterogeneous feedstock challenges.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from waste-as-cost to waste-as-onsite-energy-asset, enabled by AI process control rather than scale alone. If it matures, stores with heavy organic waste streams could pursue on-site micro-generation, altering utility contracts and back-of-house infrastructure.
candidates.author: J. P. Toomey, Rachan Karmakar, Suman Naithani et al.

candidates.title: Nighttime heat now warming faster than daytime in South Asian cities
candidates.shift: A 40-year dataset shows nighttime heat stress accelerating faster than daytime in Bangladesh's cities, undermining the assumption that night offers thermal relief.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if night no longer cools, overnight retail logistics, restocking crews and warehouse HVAC/energy-load design in hot peripheral geographies may need rethinking sooner than daytime-heat models suggest.
candidates.evidence: 1985–2024 hourly ERA5-HEAT UTCI analysis showing accelerated nighttime warming and emerging urban heat risk across Bangladesh.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from 'heat is a daytime operations problem' to 'heat risk persists around the clock,' driven by urban heat-island and climate trends. If it generalizes beyond Bangladesh, overnight labor safety standards and cooling infrastructure design for warehouses/stores in hot climates would need revision.
candidates.author: Mohammad Kamruzzaman, Abu Yousuf Md Abdullah, A. K. M. Saiful Islam et al.

candidates.title: Heat stress in heritage cities reframed as a justice issue
candidates.shift: Research on Isfahan reframes extreme heat's effect on tourism not merely as a comfort/operations problem but as a climate-justice issue for domestic visitors in Global South heritage cities.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: could push public cooling infrastructure in heritage/tourism-retail districts from optional amenity toward an equity-mandated requirement, especially in Global South cities.
candidates.evidence: Study of domestic tourist experience of thermal stress in Isfahan, examined through a climate-justice lens in a UNESCO-listed heritage core.
candidates.source: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management
candidates.initial_analysis: A reframing of heat-adaptation from technical/comfort issue to justice/equity issue. If adopted by policymakers, could mandate shaded public space and cooling infrastructure funding in heritage-retail districts across hot, non-Western tourism destinations.
candidates.author: Raymond Rastegar, Nima Soltani-Nejad, Mohammad Zamani Pirmoradi

candidates.title: Absence of a coherent global PV-waste regulatory regime
candidates.shift: A comparative review finds recycling regulation for solar-panel waste remains patchy across EU, US, China and India even as the installed PV base surges toward a major waste wave.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: retailers and warehouses with aging rooftop solar may find no clear disposal/insurance pathway — a sustainability asset that could quietly turn into an undefined liability.
candidates.evidence: Review of PV recycling regulations across Europe, US, China and India concluding preparedness for the coming PV waste stream is inadequate.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from 'solar as clean asset' to 'solar as future waste-liability without a regulatory home.' Anyone who installed rooftop solar on stores/DCs over the last decade will eventually need an end-of-life disposal category that doesn't yet fully exist.
candidates.author: Umer Shahzad, Cristina Irene Mihai, Ian Marius Peters

candidates.title: Ground-floor commercial space becomes default even in small rental housing
candidates.shift: A small collective-housing project in northern Portugal builds in a ground-floor 'store for commerce or services' as a standard feature, not a special mixed-use case.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: mixed-use ground-floor retail may be becoming a default expectation even for modest, non-urban residential builds — potentially expanding micro-retail real estate supply outside major cities.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily coverage of Collective Housing in Vila do Conde, Portugal, combining a single-family house and rental apartments with a ground-floor commercial/service unit.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from mixed-use as master-planned-tower feature to mixed-use as default even in small secondary-town housing projects. If widespread, it would quietly grow micro-format retail real estate supply outside major metros.
candidates.author: Susanna Moreira

candidates.title: Gulf builds event infrastructure for permanent legacy, not temporary use
candidates.shift: Saudi Vision 2030 expo/hospitality/entertainment districts are being designed from the outset for post-event energy, compliance and adaptive-reuse value rather than as temporary event infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: Gulf periphery may be setting a new standard where event-anchored retail/entertainment districts are engineered for decades of reuse — a template that could migrate to Western stadium-adjacent retail development.
candidates.evidence: Review of Saudi Arabia's expo, hospitality and entertainment district delivery examining energy strategy, regulatory compliance and post-event adaptation under Vision 2030.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from event infrastructure as temporary cost center to permanent regional asset class. If this Gulf approach becomes a reference model, developers of stadium/expo-adjacent retail elsewhere may need to underwrite for multi-decade adaptive reuse from day one.
candidates.author: Saquib Syed

candidates.title: Giga-projects reframed as territorial platforms, not construction jobs
candidates.shift: Saudi mega-projects are explicitly positioned as long-term regional-value platforms integrating logistics, housing, tourism and culture, rather than discrete construction programmes.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: this lifecycle/platform framing could shift how capital and long-horizon operators, including retail anchors, structure participation in giga-projects — a periphery-driven finance template.
candidates.evidence: Study of lifecycle-based regional development strategy across Saudi giga/mega projects (2020–2030) spanning infrastructure, housing, tourism and logistics corridors.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from project-based construction finance to platform-based territorial investment. Retail real-estate investors evaluating Gulf giga-projects may need new lifecycle underwriting models rather than standard single-asset deals.
candidates.author: Shahzad Jahangeer

candidates.title: Review catalogs digital-era sustainable construction technologies
candidates.shift: An academic review compiles already-known digital and sustainable construction technologies aimed at UN SDG alignment.
candidates.ai_read: Already broadly covered ground (digital twins, green materials, prefab, etc.) — included as Trend/Context, likely low new information for Kristen's map but useful as a construction-tech inventory.
candidates.evidence: Review analyzing innovative digital-revolution-driven building technologies in response to construction sector's SDG obligations.
candidates.source: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering
candidates.initial_analysis: Consolidates the ongoing shift toward digitized, sustainability-driven construction methods already underway; mostly confirms known direction rather than surfacing new signal.
candidates.author: Mais Rahdi Al-Ruwaishedi

candidates.title: Heavy-lift drones move from novelty toward real cargo capacity
candidates.shift: DARPA's Lift Challenge is demonstrating drones capable of substantial cargo lift, pushing aerial logistics beyond small-parcel delivery toward heavier freight and remote construction-material movement.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if heavy-lift drone capacity scales, it could bypass road/dock infrastructure for last-mile freight and remote-site construction delivery — directly touching the open 'delivery format?' hunt zone.
candidates.evidence: IEEE Spectrum Video Friday coverage of DARPA Lift Challenge heavy-lift drone demonstrations.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from drones-as-small-parcel-delivery to drones-as-heavy-freight-carriers. If this scales, warehouse/DC operators and remote-site builders would need to plan drone landing, charging and airspace infrastructure as a new delivery format.
candidates.author: Evan Ackerman

candidates.title: Ride-hailing's measured local-economy lift raises parking-ratio questions
candidates.shift: A Carnegie Mellon study quantifies Uber/Lyft's positive effect on local GDP and employment, strengthening the empirical case that ride-hailing measurably changes how people move through commercial areas.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative/Trend-adjacent: adds empirical weight to a known shift; worth flagging because retail site-selection and parking-ratio models built on car-ownership assumptions may be increasingly outdated.
candidates.evidence: Carnegie Mellon University study measuring GDP and employment effects of ride-hailing entry into local economies, reported by Smart Cities Dive.
candidates.initial_analysis: Confirms an already-underway shift from car-ownership-based to mobility-service-based access to retail. Site planners may need to keep re-weighting parking-lot sizing and store-accessibility models against ride-hail-driven mobility data.
candidates.author: Dan Zukowski

candidates.title: Multi-generational housing proliferates across geographies
candidates.shift: A cross-geography roundup (India, Australia, UK) shows homes increasingly designed explicitly for multi-generational living, signaling a demographic/household-formation shift toward larger, shared households.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: larger multi-generational households could shift basket size, shopping frequency and product assortment needs near residential developments, subtly reshaping neighborhood store formats.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen roundup of seven multi-generational home projects spanning India, Australia and the UK.
candidates.initial_analysis: A shift from nuclear-household to multi-generational-household design norms across diverse geographies, likely driven by housing cost and eldercare pressures. If it generalizes, retailers may need to rethink assortment and format sizing near residential clusters.
candidates.author: Starr Charles
